report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements fully defined and signed off by stakeholders, team has direct experience with React/Node stack, fixed deadline with no flexibility, scope is explicit with clear must-haves vs nice-to-haves.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build a self-service employee onboarding portal enabling new hires to complete paperwork, IT setup, and team introduction before day one.
project_understanding.beneficiary: New employees (100-200/year) and HR team (5 people)
project_understanding.trigger: Current onboarding is fragmented across PDFs and manual processes; CEO requested improvement after hearing complaints at all-hands meeting.
success_definition: 80% of onboarding tasks completable before day one
IT account setup fully automated (zero manual tickets)
supporting_quotes: Create a self-service employee onboarding portal that allows new hires to complete all required paperwork, set up their IT accounts, and get introduced to the team before day one.
Currently onboarding is fragmented - paperwork is PDF-based, IT account setup is manual, new hires feel unprepared on day one.
New hires can complete 80% of onboarding tasks before day one

hard_constraints.technology_stack: React + TypeScript (frontend), Node.js + PostgreSQL (backend), Workday API, Azure AD SSO, Azure App Service hosting

non_functional_requirements.performance: UNKNOWN - no response time targets specified
non_functional_requirements.security: SOC 2 compliance required; Azure AD SSO integration; audit logs for compliance
non_functional_requirements.usability: Self-service portal for non-technical users (new hires); accessibility not explicitly stated but required for internal tools
non_functional_requirements.data_retention: UNKNOWN - no data retention policy specified
non_functional_requirements.scalability: Expected load: 100-200 new hires/year = ~2-4 concurrent users during peak onboarding periods; modest scaling needs

assumption_log.what: Performance target: API response time < 2 seconds, page load < 3 seconds
assumption_log.why: Standard internal tool performance baseline; no explicit target given but SOC 2 compliance and user satisfaction metric (4/5) imply responsive system
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 - Quality metrics defined before build begins
assumption_log.consequence: If actual requirement is stricter (e.g., <500ms), architecture may need caching layer or CDN; if looser, over-engineering wastes budget
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows development to proceed with reasonable performance targets. Risks: if actual requirement is stricter, Phase 2-3 rework needed.

assumption_log.what: Availability target: 99.5% uptime during business hours (8am-6pm), maintenance windows allowed outside hours
assumption_log.why: Internal tool with non-critical onboarding window (new hires onboard during business hours); no explicit SLA given
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 - Quality metrics defined before build begins
assumption_log.consequence: If requirement is 99.9% or higher, infrastructure redundancy and monitoring costs increase; if lower, current plan sufficient
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows single-instance Azure App Service without premium redundancy. Risks: if higher SLA required, Phase 5 infrastructure costs increase.

assumption_log.what: Data retention: Employee onboarding records retained for 7 years (standard HR compliance window)
assumption_log.why: No explicit retention policy given; 7 years is standard for HR records under employment law
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 - Quality metrics defined before build begins
assumption_log.consequence: If actual requirement is shorter (e.g., 3 years), database design is over-provisioned; if longer (e.g., indefinite), archive strategy needed
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows database sizing and archive strategy to be planned. Risks: if wrong, Phase 3-4 rework needed for data lifecycle.

assumption_log.what: Accessibility standard: WCAG 2.1 AA (Level AA compliance)
assumption_log.why: Standard for internal tools; no explicit requirement given but SOC 2 compliance and user satisfaction metric imply accessible design
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 - Quality metrics defined before build begins
assumption_log.consequence: If requirement is AAA, additional design/testing effort needed; if no requirement, current plan sufficient
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows UX design and QA testing to proceed with clear accessibility target. Risks: if requirement is stricter, Phase 2-4 rework needed.

assumption_log.what: Workday API integration: Read-only access to employee data (name, department, manager, start date); no write-back to Workday
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'Workday API for employee data' but does not specify read vs. write scope; read-only is safer default for initial release
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 - Scope baseline requires accepted requirements
assumption_log.consequence: If write-back to Workday is required, integration complexity increases significantly; Phase 3 testing effort doubles
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: reduces integration risk and Phase 3 complexity. Risks: if write-back required, Phase 2-3 timeline extends 2-3 weeks.

assumption_log.what: Azure AD SSO: Single sign-on for new hires using corporate Azure AD tenant; no guest account provisioning needed
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'Azure AD for SSO' but does not specify guest vs. corporate account flow; corporate account is simpler for internal tool
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 - Scope baseline requires accepted requirements
assumption_log.consequence: If guest account flow required, authentication architecture changes; Phase 2 backend work increases 1-2 weeks
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: simplifies authentication implementation. Risks: if guest flow required, Phase 2 rework needed.

assumption_log.what: Document e-signature: Integration with third-party e-signature service (e.g., DocuSign, Adobe Sign); not custom-built
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'Document e-signature' but does not specify build vs. integrate; third-party integration is standard and faster
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 - Scope baseline requires accepted requirements
assumption_log.consequence: If custom e-signature required, Phase 2 effort increases significantly and compliance risk increases; third-party is safer
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: reduces development effort and compliance risk. Risks: adds third-party vendor dependency and recurring cost.

assumption_log.what: IT account provisioning: Automated provisioning to email, Slack, and SaaS tools via API calls; no manual approval step required
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'IT account setup automated (no manual tickets)' as success metric; assumes full automation without human approval
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 - Scope baseline requires accepted requirements
assumption_log.consequence: If approval step required (e.g., manager approval before provisioning), workflow complexity increases; Phase 2 design changes
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: achieves 'zero manual tickets' success metric. Risks: if approval required, Phase 2 workflow design changes.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend Developer and Frontend Developer must be allocated full-time (80%+) on critical path tasks; UX Designer front-loaded in Phase 1-2 with flexibility in Phase 3-4.

risk_register.description: If Workday API sandbox access is not granted or API contract changes, then backend development cannot proceed and Phase 2 timeline slips by 2+ weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Workday sandbox access not confirmed by end of Phase 1 Week 1
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm Workday API access in Phase 1 Task T4 before any backend development starts; document API contract in writing; establish backup plan (manual data import) if API unavailable
risk_register.contingency: If API access delayed, implement manual employee data import via CSV upload; this adds 1 week to Phase 2 but unblocks development

risk_register.description: If Azure AD SSO integration fails or tenant configuration is incorrect, then authentication flow breaks and Phase 2 development is blocked.
risk_register.trigger: Azure AD SSO test in Phase 1 Task T5 fails or IT Director cannot grant tenant access
risk_register.mitigation: Test Azure AD SSO in Phase 1 Task T5 with IT Director present; document tenant configuration requirements in writing; establish test tenant for development
risk_register.contingency: If SSO fails, implement temporary basic auth (username/password) for development; migrate to SSO in Phase 3 after IT resolves tenant issues

risk_register.description: If IT account provisioning APIs (email, Slack, SaaS tools) have rate limiting or quota restrictions, then bulk provisioning may fail and Phase 2 design must change.
risk_register.trigger: Rate limiting or quota errors discovered during Phase 3 Task T18 integration testing
risk_register.mitigation: Document rate limits and quotas for all target systems in Phase 1; design queue-based provisioning with retry logic in Phase 2 Task T13; test with production-like volume in Phase 3
risk_register.contingency: If rate limiting prevents bulk provisioning, implement staggered provisioning (queue-based with delays) or request quota increase from IT

risk_register.description: If e-signature service (DocuSign/Adobe Sign) integration is more complex than expected, then Phase 2 development effort increases and timeline slips.
risk_register.trigger: E-signature API documentation review in Phase 2 reveals unexpected complexity or missing features
risk_register.mitigation: Review e-signature service API documentation in Phase 1; select service with proven internal tool integrations; allocate 20 hours for Phase 2 Task T12 (sufficient buffer)
risk_register.contingency: If integration more complex, defer advanced features (e.g., bulk signing) to Phase 2 release; implement basic single-document signing in Phase 1

risk_register.description: If SOC 2 compliance requirements are more stringent than anticipated, then Phase 1 design and Phase 3 security review may require rework.
risk_register.trigger: Security team review in Phase 1 Task T6 or Phase 3 Task T21 identifies compliance gaps
risk_register.mitigation: Engage Security team early in Phase 1 Task T6; document all SOC 2 requirements in writing; design audit logging and data handling upfront; conduct security review in Phase 3 Task T21
risk_register.contingency: If compliance gaps found, prioritize critical controls; defer non-critical controls to Phase 2 release if needed

risk_register.description: If Backend Developer is unavailable or leaves the project, then critical path tasks (T10, T18, T22) cannot be completed and project is blocked.
risk_register.trigger: Backend Developer absence or departure announced
risk_register.mitigation: Ensure Backend Developer is allocated 80% full-time (not shared with other projects); document all critical code and architecture decisions; pair programming on critical tasks
risk_register.contingency: If Backend Developer unavailable, hire contract backend developer immediately; knowledge transfer from departing developer; timeline extends 2-3 weeks

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 requirements gathering takes longer than 2 weeks, then Phase 2 start is delayed and critical path slips.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 milestones not met by end of Week 2
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule Phase 1 kickoff immediately; set hard deadline for requirements sign-off (end of Week 2); limit scope of Phase 1 to must-haves only
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 1 extends beyond Week 2, compress Phase 2 by deferring nice-to-have features (chat bot, mobile app, LMS integration) to Phase 2 release

risk_register.description: If stakeholders request scope additions (e.g., mobile app, chat bot, LMS integration) during Phase 2-3, then timeline slips and budget overruns.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests new features or changes to existing features during Phase 2-3
risk_register.mitigation: Establish change control process in Phase 1; document nice-to-have features as Phase 2 backlog; get stakeholder sign-off on scope baseline before Phase 2 starts
risk_register.contingency: If scope additions requested, evaluate impact on timeline/budget; defer to Phase 2 release or negotiate trade-offs (e.g., drop another feature)

risk_register.description: If React/TypeScript or Node.js/PostgreSQL stack has unexpected compatibility issues, then Phase 2 development is delayed.
risk_register.trigger: Compatibility issues discovered during Phase 2 Task T7 or T8 project setup
risk_register.mitigation: Team has direct experience with React/Node stack (stated in input); use proven libraries and versions; set up development environment in Phase 2 Task T7-T8 early
risk_register.contingency: If compatibility issues found, allocate 1-2 days for troubleshooting; escalate to tech lead if unresolved

risk_register.description: If UX Designer is unavailable after Phase 2, then Phase 3-4 design refinements and accessibility audit cannot be completed.
risk_register.trigger: UX Designer absence or departure announced after Phase 2
risk_register.mitigation: UX Designer allocated 60% in Phases 1-2, 20% in Phases 3-4 (not critical path); document all design decisions and component library; defer Phase 3-4 design work if needed
risk_register.contingency: If UX Designer unavailable, hire contract designer for Phase 4 accessibility audit; defer design refinements to Phase 2 release

staffing_plan.notes: Full-time PM ownership across all phases; responsible for stakeholder alignment, requirements sign-off, UAT coordination, and post-launch adoption
Full-time allocation required; owns all backend development, integrations, security, and compliance; critical path tasks T10, T18, T22 cannot slip
Full-time allocation required; owns all frontend UI development; critical path task T14 cannot slip; responsible for responsive design and accessibility
Front-loaded in Phases 1-2 (60% allocation); reduced to 20% in Phases 3-4 for design refinements and accessibility audit; not on critical path but essential for user experience

Back-loaded in Phases 3-4; minimum 25% of development effort (272h backend + 180h frontend = 452h dev; 25% = 113h QA minimum); allocated 44h is below minimum — recommend increasing to 113h or adding second QA resource

open_questions.question: What is the exact data retention policy for employee onboarding records? (Assumption A3 assumes 7 years; confirm if different)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Database sizing, archive strategy, and compliance design depend on this; wrong assumption requires Phase 3 rework

open_questions.question: Does Workday API integration require write-back to Workday, or is read-only access sufficient? (Assumption A5 assumes read-only)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Write-back integration significantly increases Phase 2-3 complexity; wrong assumption requires 2-3 week timeline extension

open_questions.question: Does IT account provisioning require manager approval before provisioning, or is it fully automated? (Assumption A8 assumes fully automated)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Approval workflow changes Phase 2 design; wrong assumption requires workflow redesign

open_questions.question: Which e-signature service should be used (DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or other)? (Assumption A7 assumes third-party integration)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Service selection affects Phase 2 integration effort and recurring costs; decision needed before Phase 2 Task T12

open_questions.question: What is the acceptable response time target for API endpoints and page load times? (Assumption A1 assumes <2s API, <3s page load)
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Performance targets affect architecture decisions; wrong assumption may require caching/CDN in Phase 3

All hard constraints are known. Deductions reflect 8 assumptions on NFRs and scope ambiguities that are reasonable but should be validated. No CRITICAL risks present.
